name: theme
title: Theme
description: The resolved palette and colour-scheme hooks, for the places that take a colour value instead of a class name — React Navigation, status bar, native props.
author: Alejo Garcia

files.content:
/**
 * Imperative color palette for places where NativeWind classes can't reach:
 * native props (placeholderTextColor, ActivityIndicator), icon colors, the
 * React Navigation theme.
 *
 * This is a SECOND COPY of the tokens in `global.css`, and that is the whole
 * problem with it: this file used to say it was "kept in sync" by hand, and it
 * silently was not — the palette was re-themed to React Native Reusables' values
 * and this file kept the old blue, so every screen went neutral while the tab bar
 * stayed blue. Nothing failed; you had to look at the app to see it.
 *
 * `colors.test.ts` now derives these values from `global.css` and fails when the
 * two disagree, so the claim above is checked rather than asserted.
 *
 * Values are RNR's tokens converted from HSL. Do not hand-edit: change
 * `global.css` and let the test tell you what these should become.
 */
export const palette = {
  light: {
    background: '#FFFFFF', // --background: 0 0% 100%
    card: '#FFFFFF', // --card: 0 0% 100%
    foreground: '#0A0A0A', // --foreground: 0 0% 3.9%
    mutedForeground: '#737373', // --muted-foreground: 0 0% 45.1%
    primary: '#171717', // --primary: 0 0% 9%
    primaryForeground: '#FAFAFA', // --primary-foreground: 0 0% 98%
    border: '#E5E5E5', // --border: 0 0% 89.8%
    destructive: '#EF4444', // --destructive: 0 84.2% 60.2%
  },
  dark: {
    background: '#0A0A0A', // --background: 0 0% 3.9%
    card: '#0A0A0A', // --card: 0 0% 3.9%  (RNR gives cards a border, not a fill)
    foreground: '#FAFAFA', // --foreground: 0 0% 98%
    mutedForeground: '#A3A3A3', // --muted-foreground: 0 0% 63.9%
    primary: '#FAFAFA', // --primary: 0 0% 98%
    primaryForeground: '#171717', // --primary-foreground: 0 0% 9%
    border: '#262626', // --border: 0 0% 14.9%
    destructive: '#E14E4E', // --destructive: 0 70.9% 59.4%
  },
} as const;

export type ThemeColors = Record<keyof (typeof palette)['light'], string>;

docs:
`colors.ts` is a second copy of the tokens in hex, because React Navigation and native props take resolved colours rather than class names. templapp keeps the two honest with `src/theme/colors.test.ts`, which parses global.css and converts each token — copy that test too, or the palette will drift the first time you re-theme.

This item deliberately omits `theme-provider.tsx`: it reads the persisted colour-scheme preference from templapp's `@/data` store, so it only makes sense inside templapp.

Run `npx expo install --fix` — the CLI writes caret ranges, which resolve ahead of your Expo SDK matrix.
